issues.title: Impossible generalized-net depth condition

failure_location.quote:
every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $(b^{e_1},\dots,b^{e_d})$ with $e_1k_1 + \cdots + e_dk_d \le m-t$
contains exactly $b^t$ points of $P$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $m,b,t \in \NN_0$ with $m \ge 1$ and $b \ge 2$ and $e_j \in \NN$ for $1 \le j \le d$.
Let $P = \{\bsx_0, \bsx_1, \dots, \bsx_{b^m-1}\} \subset [0,1)^d$ be a set of $b^m$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition stipulates that P has b^m points but requires exactly b^t points in every interval whose weighted depth is at most m-t. For any m>t, taking every k_j=0 makes the whole cube admissible, so it must contain both b^m and b^t points. Consequently, the theorem asserting that a generalized Niederreiter sequence is a (0,e,d)-sequence is false under the old definition. Replacing the inequality by equality and restricting sequence blocks to m>=t removes the contradiction.
issues.overall_effect: The old theorem identifying generalized Niederreiter sequences as (0,e,d)-sequences fails literally, and subsequent applications of that identification to coarse gain and variance results are not established until the definition is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the generalized-net depth condition e_1k_1 + ... + e_dk_d <= m-t by equality, and state the sequence block condition only for m >= t. Under this standard reading, the cited generalized Niederreiter theorem, the mixed-base equidistribution identification, and all listed gain and variance consequences remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces equality: b^m points with b^t points per tested cell require weighted cell depth m-t, and the later claimed equivalence with mixed-base equidistribution confirms that reading. The impossible coarser cases cannot constitute a coherent promise, and no downstream argument uses the literal <= condition, so this is a transcriptional correction rather than mathematical reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $(b^{e_1},\dots,b^{e_d})$ with $e_1k_1 + \cdots + e_dk_d = m-t$
contains exactly $b^t$ points of $P$.

issues.title: Unspecified block-affine shift invalidates uniformity lemma

failure_location.quote: For a prime power $b$, the block affine matrix scramble in base $\bsb = (b^{e_1}, \dots, b^{e_d})$ is a nested scramble in base $\bsb$ and has two-fold uniformity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $1 \le j \le d$, let $\Delta_j \in \mathbb{F}_b^{\infty}$ and $M_j \in \mathbb{F}_b^{\infty \times \infty}$ be independent random vectors and matrices.

Each $M_j$ is a block lower-triangular matrix with block size $e_j$, where diagonal blocks are drawn uniformly from the nonsingular matrices in $\mathbb{F}_b^{e_j \times e_j}$, and off-diagonal blocks are drawn uniformly from all matrices in $\mathbb{F}_b^{e_j \times e_j}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the old construction Delta_j is merely called a random vector, with no distribution imposed. Taking the admissible degenerate choice Delta_j=0 makes the first output block of a zero input deterministically zero. The random invertible diagonal block cannot randomize zero, so even one-fold uniformity fails, and hence two-fold uniformity fails as well. The new iid-uniform translation supplies the missing premise.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed block-affine implementation was not certified to be unbiased or two-fold uniform as specified. Generic results that independently assume a nested scramble with two-fold uniformity remain unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify in the block affine scramble definition that every Delta_j has i.i.d. uniform entries over F_b and is independent of the matrices and other coordinate randomizations. The standard blockwise affine argument then establishes one-fold and two-fold uniformity without changing the construction or any generic scrambling result.
issues.why_classification: This is not a typo because the missing distribution is a necessary premise: the old construction permits Delta_j=0, for which uniformity fails. The repair is nevertheless a short, routine qualification directly supported by the preceding ordinary affine-scramble definition and preserves the same algorithm and guarantee, so no nontrivial new argument is needed.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The entries of each $\Delta_j$ are i.i.d.\ and uniformly distributed over $\mathbb{F}_b$.

issues.title: Gain coefficient is normalized by an extra factor of n
issues.failure_explanation: Let S denote the weighted double sum in eq:Gtilda_def. The old equations give G=S/[n^2 product_j(b_j-1)], whereas the variance theorem and subsequent gain identities require S/[n product_j(b_j-1)]. For example, in base 2 with P_2={0,1/2} and a unit-variance function depending on the second output digit, a fully nested scramble gives estimator variance 1/2. Here S=2, so the old definition gives G=1/2 and eq:variance-gain predicts 1/4. The same scaling yields G=1/n rather than item:mimic1's G=1 whenever 1<n<=m_{u,empty,k}.
issues.overall_effect: The old variance theorem and exact gain identities use incompatible gain normalizations. Later variance decompositions written with the rescaled old G require reciprocal sample-size factors when G is restored to the standard normalization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the leading factor 1/n from the definition of tilde G, so that for double sum S one has G=S/[n product_j(b_j-1)]. Retain the listed exact gain identities and bounds under this normalization, and insert the corresponding factor 1/n in each downstream variance decomposition and bound that had absorbed it into the old rescaled G. This preserves the numerical variance guarantees and convergence rates.
issues.why_classification: The old source alternates between two normalizations, so a reader cannot correct one isolated transcription and continue without propagating the convention through the affected chain. That propagation is only mechanical scalar bookkeeping: the counting arguments, gain proofs, conclusions, and rates require no new lemma or substantive weakening. The issue is therefore minor rather than moderate.

issues.title: Counting lemma omits the definition's factor n^{-2}

failure_location.quote:
Thus \eqref{eq:C_def} implies that
\[
C_{u,v,\bsk}(P_n)
= t(q+1)^2 + (m_{u,v,\bsk} - t)q^2.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: If N is the number of ordered pairs in the same relevant elementary interval, old eq:C_def gives C=N/n^2. The proof correctly counts N as t(q+1)^2+(m-t)q^2 but then identifies that raw count with C. In the at-most-one-point regime N=n, so the old definition gives C=1/n while eq:Cformula gives C=n. Removing n^{-2} makes C the raw count actually established by the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational counting lemma is false under its own definition, so the subsequent derivation of exact gain identities and all formal results relying on those identities lack a valid counting input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the factor n^{-2} from the definition of C_{u,v,k}, making C the raw number of ordered point pairs in the same relevant interval. The occupancy count in the lemma then equals C exactly, and all listed downstream gain calculations retain their existing algebraic form.
issues.why_classification: The proof, the closed formula, and subsequent uses consistently compute and use the raw ordered-pair count; the normalized meaning appears only in the defective definition and is never used in the reasoning. Thus the surrounding old source uniquely forces deletion of the factor, after which the reader can continue without changing any inference or guarantee.

issues.title: Undefined empty-set term in coarse variance decomposition
issues.failure_explanation: The old right-hand side ranges over every u subseteq 1:d, including u=empty. The gain coefficient definition explicitly applies only to nonempty u, and the ANOVA variance decomposition likewise contains only nonempty components. Thus the displayed equality contains an undefined G_{emptyset,k} term. V2 restricts both sums to nonempty u. Its added 1/n factor is instead the mechanical consequence of renormalizing G under the separate C03 root.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed base-change variance identity is not well-defined at its empty-set summand. Removing that term leaves all meaningful nonempty contributions and downstream formulas unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict both subset sums in the coarse base-change variance identity to nonempty u. This removes the undefined empty-set gain term while leaving every meaningful nonempty contribution unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The gain definition, ANOVA variance decomposition, and preceding variance theorem all explicitly range only over nonempty coordinate sets, uniquely fixing the intended scope of this display. Removing the empty term requires no mathematical argument and entails no loss because the constant ANOVA component contributes no variance.
